PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-05-18
38M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling well overall and takes his blood pressure medication each morning, checking home readings twice a week. No shortness of breath. He works as a software developer, mostly seated, and runs on weekends. Mother with rheumatoid arthritis. Appetite is good, weight stable. Sleep is about 7 hours most nights. Lives with his spouse. Never smoker, occasional alcohol.

O:
BP 124/78, HR 66, RR 14, Temp 98.2 F, SpO2 99% on room air. Weight 178 lb, BMI 25.
General: well appearing, in no distress.
HEENT: normal.
Neck: no lymphadenopathy, no thyromegaly.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur, no gallop.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: soft, nontender, no organomegaly.
Extremities: no edema, joints without swelling, pulses intact.
Labs (prior week): basic metabolic panel normal, lipid panel within goal, A1c 5.3%.

A/P:
1. Essential hypertension, well controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg daily. Home readings reviewed, averaging 122/76. Repeat basic metabolic panel in 12 months.
2. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed age-appropriate screening and reassurance.
3. Health maintenance: discussed age-appropriate preventive care and immunizations, which are up to date. Encouraged continued weekend running and adding light strength exercises twice weekly.
4. Lifestyle: reviewed balanced meals, limiting sodium, and taking regular breaks from prolonged sitting during the workday. Discussed consistent sleep and adequate hydration.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner as needed.
